quote: actually, the other thing too is we are I am tied into one of those, like, solar farms where they give you, like, a percentage of the, you know, they're kind of associated with Excel sort of.
stewart_read: Customer discloses participation in a community-solar/subscription program tied to Xcel, a scenario not covered in Ion's script. The rep's response is a generic acknowledgment rather than a probe into how this affects his usage or offset calculation.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have intentionally avoided engaging with the topic to stay within setter scope, deferring the technical implications to the closer — a defensible strategic move given setter_scope_discipline.
coaching_implication: This is likely a genuine schema content gap (Kenny should be asked whether community-solar subscriptions affect Ion's design process) rather than purely a rep miss — flag for schema expansion, and coach the rep to at minimum note it clearly for the closer's benefit rather than a bare acknowledgment.

quote: Okay. Yes. Sounds good. No problem. I'll go ahead and put that down here. I appreciate you for letting me know.
stewart_read: The rep files the solar-farm disclosure as data without reflecting it back or using it to build anticipation for what the closer will show him — a missed hook given curiosity_over_features guidance.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't know what to do with this out-of-script detail. Strategic read is weak here since there's no indication the rep intentionally deferred it for later use in the call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect novel disclosures back to the customer ('that's helpful context, our specialist will factor that into your design') rather than a flat acknowledgment — costs nothing and signals attentiveness.

quote: Probably afternoon. I think my wife would wanna be there. She works in a Saturday morning.
stewart_read: The customer, not the rep, surfaces that his wife needs to be present. The rep never proactively asked whether Tamara (identified earlier as co-title-holder) should be on the appointment — this wasn't a spouse objection to overcome, so the schema's objection-handling frame doesn't strictly apply, but the rep also never confirmed her by name or made a deliberate move to include her.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep's later line 'work good for you and your wife?' shows he retained the Tamara detail and folded her into the time-lock, suggesting passive but adequate tracking rather than active protocol execution.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to proactively name the co-owner and confirm their attendance right when co-owner is disclosed (04:06-04:14), rather than relying on the customer to raise it — the appointment held here, but the rep didn't drive the inclusion, the customer did.

quote: I'll probably just email it to you. I'm I'm at work now, so I gotta it'll probably take a little bit to dig that up.
stewart_read: No dollar bill amount is ever captured on this call — only the commitment to send usage data later. This leaves the pitch without an emotional anchor to the customer's actual pain point.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since this appears to be a referral/warm lead already motivated by a family connection, the rep may have judged that bill-pain anchoring was less necessary to secure the booking, which the outcome supports.
coaching_implication: Even on warm referral leads, ask for a ballpark bill number verbally before moving to bill-document collection — it costs 10 seconds and gives the closer a stronger opening anchor regardless of lead warmth.

quote: you have some free time either tomorrow or Friday.
stewart_read: Rep offers concrete near-term options quickly, and when the customer counters with a Saturday request, the rep checks the calendar and locks a specific day and time within a few exchanges — efficient handling of a scheduling countermove.
coaching_implication: This is a positive pattern worth reinforcing — quick calendar-check and confirm rather than stalling when a customer proposes an alternate day.

quote: I'll, I'll block off that spot for an hour just to ensure you guys don't feel rushed as well.
stewart_read: Rep hits the one-hour-block button-up element clearly, a required element that's often skipped on other calls in the corpus.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as a habit already working well; no action needed beyond noting it.

quote: we'll shoot for this Saturday at 2PM.
stewart_read: The call closes with a restated time but no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake or no-driving/computer instruction — the button-up is missing its verbal-commitment mechanic even though the date/time itself is locked.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may consider the customer's immediate 'Alright. Sounds great. Thanks for your help.' as sufficient confirmation, making the formal handshake redundant in this specific warm-referral context.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add the explicit no-driving/computer instruction and the 'is that fair?' handshake even on easy, cooperative calls — procedural completeness protects show-rate regardless of how warm the customer sounds.
